A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spark3D study. Their text, tables, figures and supplied appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison after matching retained and relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original MRI segmentation experiments, development ablations and generalization analyses, plus the authors' BTCV CT evaluations in Appendix C.2 and Table 11.

after.justification: V3 reports original MRI and CT segmentation results and ablations, including the retained main test results and the development comparison in Table 2(c).

M1.justification: The ResEnc U-Net architecture, masked L2 reconstruction objective, sparsification and densification components, dynamic 60–90% masking, and selected fine-tuning procedure are retained. The revised freezing description does not establish an actual method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the clinical MRI collection, ABCD pre-training, downstream datasets D1–D13 and BTCV CT segmentation. Correcting Table 2(c) and removing one model configuration from Table 9 do not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 includes VoCo, VolumeFusion and Models Genesis in the development comparison in Table 2(c), where v2 instead duplicated the ABCD checkpoint comparison from Table 5. Main test and CT comparator sets remain unchanged. AMAES receives new discussion but is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the stated encoder-freezing control from the entire fine-tuning process to the warm-up process. Table 3's schedules and results remain unchanged, indicating a reported protocol correction rather than evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 9 drops S3D-L from the modality- and patient-shift analyses, reducing evidence about longer pre-training under these shifts. Both scenarios remain, as do the other ablations and the broader long-schedule comparison in Table 12.

E5.justification: Bootstrap ranking distributions in Figure 2 and five-fold results with standard deviations in Table 8 are retained. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty reporting practices or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: Corrected Table 2(c) adds development results for VoCo, VF and MG, with mean DSCs of 68.77, 70.31 and 71.18, alongside retained S3D results of 71.65. The displaced ABCD results remain in Table 5. Table 9 removes S3D-L's 26.90, 72.53 and 64.95 entries; main test results in Table 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Mathematical descriptions of reconstruction, masking and sampling are unchanged. Neither version provides a formal theoretical contribution, and v3 adds no definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: carefully configured CNN MAE pre-training, comprehensive evaluation, and approximately three Dice points over dynamic nnU-Net. Additional evidence and qualifications do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Table 2(b)'s caption changes dynamic masking from performing best to performing similarly. Table 6 explicitly excepts D4 from the claim that 40 cases nearly match full-data training. Section 4 attributes the freezing conclusion to early exploratory work. These qualify interpretations of existing results.

D1.justification: V3 discloses NSD's 2 mm tolerance, exact train/validation/test counts and validation-set reporting in Table 6, and S3D-Long use on validation splits in Table 10. The abstract's code link changes from an anonymous repository to MIC-DKFZ/nnssl, and Appendix E adds ABCD provenance.

R1.justification: New Appendix D contrasts AMAES's evaluation coverage, low-data setting and single-channel baselines with this work. Citations to Chaitanya et al., Gu et al., Valanarasu et al. and the ABCD study are added. These are targeted expansions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, including ABCD's name, adds Maximilian Miller and revises affiliations, and introduces acknowledgments and Appendices D–E. The main scientific section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2(c) is rebuilt with methods as rows and development datasets as columns. Table 9 loses a column, several captions expand, and appendix tables are relocated. Figures 1–3 retain their content, with modest resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Replacing v2's mismatched Table 2(c), qualifying the masking and low-data interpretations, and documenting existing evaluation settings improve clarity and reproducibility. Removing S3D-L's Table 9 results slightly reduces generalization evidence, although Table 12 retains its broader evaluation. The net gain is limited but supported; the main method and test results remain unchanged.
